h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ב׳ Pesach — Maamar Bais
Bread over Which Much Is Answered: Feeling the Exodus Anew

p: בַּגְּמָרָא
In the Gemara
(פְּסָחִים קט"ו:):
(Pesachim 115b):
לֶחֶם עֹנִי — שֶׁעוֹנִין עָלָיו דְּבָרִים הַרְבֵּה.
"Bread of affliction (oni)—over which many things are answered (onin)."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת דֶּרֶךְ שְׁאֵלָה וּתְשׁוּבָה:
That is, it must be conducted by way of question and answer:
הַבֵּן שׁוֹאֵל מַה נִּשְׁתַּנָּה וְאָבִיו מְשִׁיבוֹ,
the son asks "Why is this night different?" and his father answers him,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
and as they said
(שָׁם קט"ז.):
(ibid. 116a):
בְּנוֹ שׁוֹאֲלוֹ וְכוּלֵּי אִשְׁתּוֹ שׁוֹאֶלְתּוֹ וְאִם לָאו הוּא שׁוֹאֵל לְעַצְמוֹ.
"His son asks him, etc.; his wife asks him; and if not, he asks himself."
וְכֵן בְּמַאֲמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
And similarly in the statement of Rabban Gamliel:
מַצָּה שֶׁאָנוּ אוֹכְלִין עַל שׁוּם מָה וְכוּלֵּי, מָרוֹר עַל שׁוּם מָה וְכוּלֵּי
"This matzah that we eat, for what reason? etc.; this maror, for what reason? etc."
וְאֵין אוֹמְרִים סְתָם מַצָּה שֶׁאָנוּ אוֹכְלִין עַל שׁוּם שֶׁלֹּא הִסְפִּיק וְכוּלֵּי, רַק דֶּרֶךְ שְׁאֵלָה וּתְשׁוּבָה
and we do not simply state "Matzah that we eat is because [the dough] did not have time, etc.," rather by way of question and answer
(וְכֵן הוּא גִּירְסַת הָרֹא"שׁ).
(and such is the reading of the Rosh).
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבַּלַּיְלָה צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לְהַרְגִּישׁ בְּנַפְשׁוֹ חֲדָשׁוֹת,
And this is because on this night a person must feel something new within his soul,
שֶׁצָּרִיךְ הָאָדָם לִרְאוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ כְּאִילּוּ הוּא יָצָא מִמִּצְרַיִם וְכוּלֵּי,
for a person must view himself as though he personally went out of Egypt, etc.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז הִרְגִּישׁ אָדָם בְּנַפְשׁוֹ הֶרְגֵּשׁ חָזָק שֶׁיָּצָא מִן הַמֵּיצַר,
That is, back then a person felt in his soul a powerful sensation of emerging from straits,
וְכֵן צָרִיךְ כָּל אָדָם לְהַרְגִּישׁ בְּכָל לֵיל פֶּסַח כְּאִילּוּ הוּא יָצָא מִמִּצְרַיִם,
and similarly every person must feel on every Pesach night as though he personally went out of Egypt,
וְלֹא יִהְיֶה הַדָּבָר אֶצְלוֹ כְּדָבָר הֶרְגֵּל לֶאֱכוֹל מַצָּה וּמָרוֹר וְכַדּוֹמֶה.
so that eating matzah and maror and the like should not be to him a matter of mere habit.
וְכֵן כָּל עִיקַּר תַּקָּנַת טִיבּוּל רִאשׁוֹן אָמְרוּ שֶׁהִיא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלִיהֱוֵי הֶכֵּירָא לְתִינוֹקוֹת
And likewise, the entire essence of the enactment of the first dipping they said is so that there be a noticeable distinction for the children
(שָׁם קי"ד:),
(ibid. 114b),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּתְעוֹרֵר הָאָדָם: מַה נִּשְׁתַּנָּה הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה מִכָּל הַלֵּילוֹת,
meaning that a person should be aroused to ask, "Why is this night different from all other nights?"
שֶׁיֵּשׁ שִׁינּוּי בָּזֶה וְיָצָא מֵהֶרְגֵּל.
that there is a change here and one steps out of routine.
וּבָא הַשְּׁאֵלָה רִאשׁוֹנָה עַל טִיבּוּל יְרָקוֹת,
And the first question comes concerning the dipping of vegetables,
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה קִלְלַת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
for this was the curse of Adam HaRishon,
שֶׁמִּקּוֹדֶם הָיָה מַאֲכַל אָדָם רַק פְּרִי הָעֵץ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְקַלֵּל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן: וְאָכַלְתָּ אֶת עֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה,
as previously man's food was only the fruit of the tree, and afterward Adam HaRishon was cursed: "And you shall eat the grass of the field,"
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהִזִּיעוּ פָּנָיו וְאָמַר: אֲנִי וַחֲמוֹרִי נֹאכַל בְּאֵבוּס אֶחָד?
and once his face sweated and he said, "Shall I and my donkey eat from one trough?"
אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: הוֹאִיל וְהִזִּיעוּ פָּנֶיךָ תֹּאכַל לֶחֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה
the Holy One, blessed is He, said to him, "Since your face sweated, you shall eat bread," as they said in Bereishis Rabbah
וְכָאן בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם אַחַר מַכָּה עֲשִׂירִית, שֶׁיָּצְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִכָּל עֶשֶׂר הַקְּלִיפּוֹת וְנִכְנְסוּ לְעֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת דִּקְדוּשָּׁה
And here at the Exodus from Egypt, after the tenth plague, when Israel emerged from all ten husks and entered the ten attributes of holiness
שֶׁכֵּן הָיוּ עֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת נָגוֹף לְמִצְרַיִם וְרָפוֹא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר
for indeed the ten plagues were "smiting for Egypt and healing for Israel," as brought in the Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' ל"ו.)
הִתְחִיל הַתִּיקּוּן לִפְגַם אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן.
the rectification for the blemish of Adam HaRishon began.
וְצָרִיךְ לְהַרְגִּישׁ הַשִּׁינּוּי שֶׁיְּתוּקַּן הַכֹּל וְלֹא יִהְיֶה שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה,
And one must feel the transformation that everything be rectified and there be no leaven in the dough;
וְזֶה צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לְהַרְגִּישׁ בְּכָל לֵיל פֶּסַח הֶרְגֵּשׁ מְחוּדָּשׁ וְשִׁינּוּי,
and this a person must feel on every Pesach night—a renewed sensation and change,
שֶׁלַּיְלָה זוֹ מְשׁוּנָּה מִכָּל הַלֵּילוֹת, שֶׁבָּזֶה מַרְגִּישׁ כְּאִילּוּ הוּא יָצָא מִמִּצְרַיִם.
that this night is different from all nights, whereby he feels as though he personally went out of Egypt.
וְאַף דְּאַכַּתִּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן,
And even though "we are still servants of Ahasuerus,"
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַלְלוּ עַבְדֵי ה' וְלֹא עַבְדֵי פַרְעֹה,
nevertheless "they are servants of Hashem and not servants of Pharaoh,"
שֶׁמִּזֶּה כְּבָר יָצָאנוּ, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה שִׁיעְבּוּד כָּזֶה כְּמוֹ בְּמִצְרַיִם שֶׁהִקִּיפָה הַקְּלִיפָּה מִכָּל צַד,
for from that we have already departed, so that there is no longer such subjugation as in Egypt where the husk surrounded them on every side,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(דְּבָרִים ד', ל"ד):
(Devarim 4:34):
גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי
"a nation from the midst of a nation"
כְּעוּבָּר בִּמְעֵי אִמּוֹ.
like a fetus in its mother's womb.
וּמִזֶּה כְּבָר יָצָאנוּ, וְצָרִיךְ אָדָם לְהַרְגִּישׁ בְּכָל שָׁנָה יְצִיאָה מְחוּדֶּשֶׁת כְּאִילּוּ הוּא יָצָא מִמִּצְרַיִם.
From that we have already emerged, and a person must feel every year a renewed exodus as though he personally went out of Egypt.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, First Night of Pesach 3 — “Hashem set the shining of the salvation of Pesach to come by way of question, as it is written, ‘When your son asks you tomorrow, What is this?’; and the Sages further instituted changes on this night more than on all nights, so that onlookers will wonder and a question will be aroused in their hearts. For at the Exodus Hashem began to open the light fully, so that it appears in human grasp up to the point that stands to question and answer; therefore He made this salvation shine by way of difficulty and question. So we make changes on it, to ask and to answer, to teach that one must always set in the heart a question and an outcry, and through this the salvation is awakened even before its time.” Connection: The same insistence that the night run by question and answer, with changes made to provoke the question; it makes the question itself an outcry that hastens redemption.

paragraphs.text: Rosh, Pesachim 10:30 (the Rosh's text of the Mishnah, 116a–b) — "Pesach that our fathers ate — for what reason? Because the Omnipresent passed over our fathers' houses in Egypt… Maror — for what reason? Because the Egyptians embittered our fathers' lives… Matzah — for what reason? Because our fathers' dough had no time to leaven…" Our Gemara's Mishnah states the reasons without the question.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefas Emes, Chanukah 5660 — “The Gemara says that on Purim we do not say Hallel because ‘we are still servants of Achashverosh.’ One must understand: on the other festivals too, which recall the Exodus, we are still servants of Edom, yet we say ‘Praise, servants of Hashem,’ and not servants of the kings of the nations. But on those days on which such a redemption took place, freedom is awakened in the souls of Israel, and they are now called servants of Hashem and not servants of others. For one cannot complete the Hallel except at a time of freedom; and on these times the kingship of Heaven rests upon us, and then we are filled with song and praise.” Connection: The Sefas Emes meets the same objection, that Israel is still in exile, with the same answer, that the Exodus is renewed in the soul each time its day returns; he adds that this renewed freedom is what makes the full Hallel possible.
